narrative:
The model estimated a 67% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that risk was above the school’s threshold, your application was rejected. This is not a judgment of your ability, but an assessment based mainly on your academic record.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That low standing pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing was also in the lowest decile, again far below the accepted average, and it added further risk. Your LSAT score of 36, compared with an accepted average of about 37, was only modestly below average and was the one top factor that leaned toward passing, but it was not strong enough to outweigh the concerns about your class standing.

To move forward, ask the admissions office for feedback, consider whether retaking the LSAT or completing rigorous additional coursework could strengthen your record, and discuss conditional or later-cycle admission. Applying to a broader set of schools or after improving your academic evidence would be reasonable next steps.
